doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: The Shrine band and a forgotten trumpeter
summary: Talk about John Cummings, Roger Eckers, Gap Mangione and an Italian trumpeter remembered from the Shrine band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Because they would hire all of us then — and the other two guys maybe that normally played, so we would split it whenever there was two of us there. And when there were four of us there, like for some other show, like a dinner theater that wasn’t the normal, the War Memorial or the — what was it, the Shrine Auditorium. Oooh lookit, who’s this? And then he’d give you the finger. John Cummings. Do you remember him?
He led the Shrine band, and I was mortified. He was crazy.
He was a good musician. You know who was the best though? Oh boy. The guy that was a car dealer and he played trumpet? De — de something. He was amazing. He played in the Shrine band.
Did you happen to know Roger Eckers?
Yeah, he was my private teacher.

Oh wow. Roger — and you talk about somebody who was an operator. Roger tried to get around town man, with Gap Mangione, and between those two — but what was that guy’s name, oh boy, Italian guy, it was an Italian guy. Played — I never heard anybody like that. The only time I ever really heard him play was in the Shrine band once and he © Fillius Jazz Archive -29-

played like a Harry James song, oh it was just great. And I heard him play with the Shrine band, at the Shrine Circus. And I was playing in the circus band, right? And I hear — and at the Shrine, they would go all around the inner circle of the circus and play you know marches and stuff. But you know most of the people in the Shrine band couldn’t do the circus part. It was too hard. And boy I wish I could remember. This is terrible. I’m getting senile.
